name: Flinders Back Beach
signature: Raw, wild, and largely undiscovered — the best surf scenery on the eastern Peninsula with dramatic basalt rock formations
editorNote:
Flinders Back Beach is the Peninsula's hidden surf spot — less visited than Gunnamatta or Rye, more dramatic than both, and set against a backdrop of dark basalt cliffs and rock platforms that make it feel genuinely remote even though the Flinders village is five minutes away.

The swell is real Bass Strait with a slight easterly component that gives it a different character to the western beaches. On a clean south or south-east swell it produces excellent waves across multiple banks. The rock platforms at low tide are worth exploring even if you are not surfing.

Patrolled by Flinders SLSC on weekends and public holidays in summer. One of the most underrated beach walks on the Peninsula runs east from here toward Mushroom Reef Marine Sanctuary — worth 90 minutes of your time.
whyWeGo: The Peninsula's most dramatic back beach — dark basalt cliffs, real surf, and none of the crowds.
ifOnlyOneThing: Walk the coastal track east toward Mushroom Reef at low tide.
